---
name: agent-job-secrets
description: Use to list or retrieve agent job secrets, API keys, and OAuth credentials (auto-refreshed). Trigger when the user mentions a secret/credential by name, or asks "what secrets are available", "get the X token", "fetch the Y API key", or when a previously-fetched credential stops working and needs to be re-fetched.
---

## Usage

```bash
# List available secret keys (fetches current list from server)
node skills/agent-job-secrets/agent-job-secrets.js list

# Get a secret value (OAuth credentials are auto-refreshed)
node skills/agent-job-secrets/agent-job-secrets.js get MY_CREDENTIALS
```

## Notes

- `AGENT_JOB_TOKEN` and `APP_URL` are injected automatically — no setup required.
- Plain (non-OAuth) secrets are also available directly as env vars (e.g. `echo $MY_KEY`).
- OAuth credentials must be fetched via `get` — they are not available as env vars.
- `get` on an OAuth credential refreshes it server-side and returns a fresh access token.
- If a fetched credential stops working (expired token, 401 error), call `get` again to obtain a fresh one.
- `list` always fetches from the server, so it reflects secrets added after the container started.

EDGE Critical Minerals Intel — Weekly Brief

Date: 27 May 2026 | Report Period: 25–27 May 2026 | Week 3 | Classification: For EDGE Team Internal Use

Executive Summary
  • Lithium corrects 14% from highs: GFEX futures fell to ¥168,960/t (from ¥205,260 peak on May 13) as supply-restart announcements from Mt Holland, Mt Marion, and Bald Hill spooked the market, though underlying demand remains robust (+55.6% YoY battery output).
  • Cobalt holds at $56,290/t as DRC quotas continue to constrain supply. Nickel at $18,560/t, steady after Indonesia's mining quota cuts. Sulfuric acid crisis from China's export ban threatens SX-EW copper and HPAL nickel processing costs.
  • Copper faces structural deficit with JPMorgan warning of a 330,000-ton shortfall in 2026. LME copper at $13,624/t. AI data centres alone expected to consume ~475kt in 2026.
  • JPMorgan warns of 330,000-ton copper shortfall in 2026 as AI and EV demand outpace supply growth. DARPA launches SMART program for strategic materials at University of Utah.
  • Resource nationalism accelerates — Zimbabwe export quotas, DRC cobalt restrictions, Indonesia nickel cuts, and expanded Chinese REE controls create compounding supply chain pressure across multiple minerals simultaneously.

1. Market Movements

Lithium CORRECTING

Battery-grade Li₂CO₃: GFEX most-traded futures at ¥168,960/t (down 14% from May 13 peak of ¥205,260/t). Spot index at ~¥179,700/t.

Supply-side headwinds (bearish for prices):

  • Mount Holland (Australia): Expansion approved — doubling capacity to 4.4M t/yr spodumene (SQM & Wesfarmers).
  • Mt Marion (Australia): FID reached for $490M AUD flotation plant + underground mine (MinRes & Ganfeng).
  • Bald Hill (Australia): Mineral Resources restarting after 18-month suspension.
  • Core Lithium (Finniss): Restarting operations.
  • SEMCORP (Malaysia): Terminated $2B lithium-ion battery separator project — supply-side negative.

Supply-side support (bullish for prices):

  • Zimbabwe concentrate export quotas still in effect — no shipments arriving in China until late July.
  • Jiangxi (Yichun) clay mines: 4 undergoing license renewal — ~7,500 t/yr LCE at risk.
  • Greenbushes FY2026 guidance cut by ~20kt LCE (1.375–1.425M t vs 1.5–1.65M t previously).
  • Chile lithium salt exports fell 5.1% MoM in April.

Demand: China April battery output 183.9 GWh (+55.6% YoY). May schedules +10.5% MoM. LFP cathode output +72% YoY. Energy storage now 31% of lithium demand (up from 23%).

Outlook: Market digesting supply-restart news. Analyst targets: CITIC ¥250k/t (2–3 months), UBS ¥298k/t. Near-term resistance at ¥190–210k range on tight physical market.

Rare Earth Elements STRUCTURAL RISK

China's export control regime: Expanded controls on 12 REEs (adding Ho, Er, Tm, Eu, Yb) with extraterritorial reach remain suspended until November 10, 2026 — but the legal architecture is fully intact. Separation capacity remains the strategic chokepoint: China controls ~90% of global separation/refining and ~93% of magnet production.

  • DARPA "SMASH" Program: 48-month, two-phase program aiming to recover all ~80 stable elements from ore with near-zero waste. Using technologies from microbial fluids to plasma thrusters. Proposals due April 2025, program start September 2025.
  • Ucore RapidSX: Column-based separation (~3× faster than conventional). US DoD $4M demonstration + $18M Louisiana facility. Canada $36M commitment.
  • Price bifurcation: Ex-China processed REEs command 4–6× Chinese domestic prices.
  • NdPr: Elevated on US defense stockpiling via Project Vault.

Key insight: Full decoupling from Chinese processing is unrealistic before 2030. Western separation efforts are real but early-stage. November 2026 deadline is the single most consequential near-term catalyst for heavy REE supply chains.

Cobalt & Nickel SUPPLY CONSTRICTED

2. Geopolitical Developments

US–China Critical Minerals Rivalry

  • Post-Trump-Xi tactical pause: No structural reset. China's rare earth controls remain in place; US advancing Project Vault and bilateral frameworks.
  • FORGE Initiative (Feb 2026): 54 countries + EU, succeeding Minerals Security Partnership. Korea first rotating chair.
  • Project Vault: $120B strategic critical minerals stockpile announced by USTR. Minimum pricing / tariff walls under discussion.
  • 21 bilateral CRM frameworks signed since Trump's return; 17 more under negotiation.
  • China's 15th Five-Year Plan expected to prioritise strategic materials self-sufficiency.

Resource Nationalism Wave

Synchronised export restrictions on five fronts:

  • DRC: Cobalt export quotas — 96,600 t/yr for 2026–2027 (~55% cut).
  • Indonesia: Nickel mining quotas cut ~30%; Eramet Weda Bay offline.
  • Zimbabwe: Lithium ore export quotas; full export ban from 2027.
  • Namibia: Ban on exporting unprocessed critical minerals; proposed 51% local ownership.
  • China: Expanded REE controls to 12 elements; extraterritorial reach suspended only.

Russia & Central Asia

  • Russia consolidating Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan) as secure resource hinterland for uranium, copper, rare metals.
  • India reduced Russian crude imports by ~800,000 bpd since October 2025 under US pressure.
  • Three spheres of influence emerging: China in Africa, US in Americas/Greenland, Russia in Central Asia — Europe structurally outside all three.

3. Policy & Regulation

United States

  • One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025): $5B Industrial Base Fund, $2B National Defense Stockpile Fund, $500M/project Critical Minerals Loan Program.
  • Defense Production Act: $550.4M FY2025 — routed through Dept of War. 10 CRM companies supported since Jan 2025.
  • MP Materials deal: $400M equity + $150M loan for heavy REE separation at Mountain Pass, CA. 10-year NdPr floor of $110/kg. 100% offtake for magnet production.
  • Critical Minerals List expanded to 60: boron, copper, lead, met coal, phosphates, potash, rhenium, silicon, silver, uranium added.
  • January 2026 proclamation: 180-day deadline (July 13, 2026) for processed critical mineral trade deals — potential tariffs if unmet.
  • DOE Critical Minerals Accelerator: $69M NOFO for industry-led pilot/demo projects (April 2026).

European Union

  • CRMA: 47 strategic projects inside EU (€22.5B capital) + 13 international (€5.5B).

# EDGE Critical Minerals Intel — Weekly Brief
**Date:** 2026-05-27
**Report Period:** May 25–27, 2026
**Week:** 3

## Executive Summary

- **Lithium corrects 14% from ¥205k peak** as supply-restart announcements (Mt Holland, Mt Marion, Bald Hill, Finniss) spook the market. GFEX futures at ¥168,960/t, spot at ~¥179,700/t. Underlying battery demand remains robust (+55.6% YoY) but supply psychology has shifted bearish.
- **Cobalt holds at $56,290/t**, flat w/w, as DRC quotas continue to constrain supply. Nickel steady at $18,560/t. Sulfuric acid crisis (China export ban + Strait of Hormuz) threatens SX-EW copper output and HPAL nickel processing costs.
- **JPMorgan warns of 330,000-ton copper shortfall** in 2026 — AI data centres (~475kt demand), EV scaling, and grid modernisation driving a "triple demand threat." LME copper at $13,624/t. TC/RC benchmark at $0/t.
- **DARPA launches SMART program** for strategic materials at University of Utah. DOE's $69M Critical Minerals Accelerator NOFO opens for industry-led pilot/demo projects. Nth Cycle + Ionic Rare Earths partnership to replace Chinese oxalic acid in REE refining.
- **Resource nationalism continues on five fronts** — DRC cobalt quotas, Indonesia nickel cuts, Zimbabwe lithium quotas, Namibia raw mineral export ban, China expanded REE controls — creating compounding supply chain pressure across minerals.

---

## 1. Market Movements

### Lithium
- **GFEX LC2606 futures**: ¥168,960/t (down 14% from May 13 peak of ¥205,260/t). **Spot battery-grade**: ~¥179,700/t.
- **Warehouse warrants accumulating**: ~132,000 t on GFEX (+28%), contributing to bearish sentiment.
- **Supply-restart wave**: Mt Holland expansion approved (4.4M t/yr, 2× current); Mt Marion FID ($490M AUD for flotation plant + underground mine); Bald Hill restart after 18 months; Core Lithium Finniss restarting; SEMCORP terminated $2B Malaysia separator project.
- **Bullish supply factors still active**: Zimbabwe export quotas (no ore until late July); Jiangxi clay mine license renewals (7,500 t/yr LCE at risk); Greenbushes FY2026 cut by ~20kt LCE; Chile exports -5.1% MoM.
- **Demand**: April battery output 183.9 GWh (+55.6% YoY); May +10.5% MoM. ESS now 31% of lithium demand.
- **Analyst divergence**: CITIC ¥250k/t in 2–3 months; UBS ¥298k/t. Market consensus shifting toward near-term pullback then medium-term bullish.

### Rare Earth Elements
- **China's expanded controls (12 REEs)**: Suspended until November 10, 2026 — legal architecture intact. Extraterritorial "50% penetration rule" applies to foreign entities using Chinese-origin materials.
- **Separation bottleneck**: China controls ~90% of global separation capacity, ~93% of magnet production. Non-China buildout faces 5–10 year timelines.
- **DARPA "SMASH" Program**: 48-month, two-phase program to recover all ~80 stable elements from ore with near-zero waste.
- **Ucore RapidSX**: $4M DoD demonstration + $18M Louisiana facility. Column-based separation ~3× faster.
- **Nth Cycle + Ionic Rare Earths**: Electro-extraction to replace oxalic acid (sourced from China) in REE refining. Integration at Belfast facility from Q4 2026.
- **Price bifurcation**: Ex-China processed REEs command 4–6× Chinese domestic prices. NdPr elevated on US defense stockpiling.

### Cobalt & Nickel
- **Cobalt (LME)**: $56,290/t (flat w/w). DRC 96,600 t/yr export quota (~55% cut) continues to drive structural deficit of 36,000–91,000 t projected for 2026.
- **Nickel (LME)**: $18,560/t (flat w/w). Indonesia mining quotas cut ~30% (379M → 260–270M wmt). Eramet Weda Bay remains offline.
- **Sulfuric acid crisis**: China banned H₂SO₄ exports (May 1), threatening HPAL nickel processing costs in Indonesia.
- **Battery chemistry**: LFP now ~81% of China power battery installations. High-nickel NCM remains essential for premium EVs.

### Copper
- **LME Copper**: $13,624/t (down $44 w/w). Near record highs.
- **Deficit estimates**: JPMorgan 330kt, UBS >400kt, ICSG ~150kt for 2026.
- **Demand**: AI data centres ~475kt in 2026 (+110kt YoY). EVs use 3–4× copper vs ICE. Grid modernisation accelerating globally. S&P Global projects 50% demand increase by 2040 (28M → 42M tonnes).
- **Supply**: Ore grades declining below 0.6%. New mines take ~17 years from discovery to production. Grasberg force majeure, Kamoa-Kakula guidance slashed. TC/RC 2026 annual benchmark at $0/t; spot at negative $45–70/t.

### Graphite & Battery Minerals
- **Natural graphite**: Flake prices depressed (~$800–1,200/t). Supply growth (966kt → 1.6Mt) outpacing demand.
- **Synthetic graphite**: Prices trending modestly upward (~$2,500–4,000/t) on tight capacity and rising coke costs.
- **China control**: ~90% of global anode production, ~98% of graphitization capacity.
- **US anti-dumping**: 93.5% on Chinese anode-grade graphite (July 2025) — procurement patterns not yet shifted.
- **Northern Graphite**: Moved majority of spot sales to Metalshub (March 2026) — signal of non-Chinese price discovery.
- **Sodium-ion**: CATL targeting 40 GWh capacity by end-2026; could reduce graphite demand intensity at the margin.

---

## 2. Geopolitical Developments

### US–China Rivalry
- **FORGE Initiative**: 54 countries + EU, succeeding Minerals Security Partnership. Korea first rotating chair.
- **Project Vault**: $120B strategic stockpile. Minimum pricing/tariff walls under discussion by USTR.
- **21 bilateral CRM frameworks** signed since Trump's return; 17 more under negotiation.
- **MP Materials**: $400M DoW investment + $150M loan for heavy REE separation at Mountain Pass. 10-year NdPr floor of $110/kg.
- **China's 15th Five-Year Plan** expected to prioritise strategic materials self-sufficiency, reducing technology transfer.

### Resource Nationalism Wave
- **Synchronised restrictions**: DRC (cobalt quotas), Indonesia (nickel cuts), Zimbabwe (lithium quotas), Namibia (raw mineral export ban + 51% local ownership proposal), China (REE controls).
- **OECD**: Export restrictions on critical minerals increased ~5× between 2009–2024.
- **"Third pole" emerging**: African leadership aligning with Middle Eastern capital (Saudi Arabia, UAE) to build processing capabilities outside US-China binary.
- **G20 Critical Minerals Framework** (2025 Johannesburg) formally endorsed "beneficiation at source."

### Russia & Central Asia
- Russia consolidating Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan) as secure resource hinterland for uranium, copper, rare metals.
- India cut Russian crude imports by ~800,000 bpd since Oct 2025 under US pressure.
- Three spheres of influence: China in Africa, US in Americas/Greenland, Russia in Central Asia — Europe structurally outside all three.

---

## 3. Policy & Regulation

### United States
- **One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025)**: $5B Industrial Base Fund, $2B National Defense Stockpile Fund, $500M/project Critical Minerals Loan Program.
- **Defense Production Act**: $550.4M FY2025 (up from $209.2M FY2024). Dept of War now lead agency.
- **Critical Minerals List expanded to 60**: boron, copper, lead, met coal, phosphates, potash, rhenium, silicon, silver, uranium added.
- **Jan 2026 proclamation**: 180-day deadline (July 13, 2026) for processed critical mineral trade deals — potential tariffs.
- **DOE Critical Minerals Accelerator**: $69M NOFO (April 2026) for industry-led pilot/demo projects. Topic Area 2: Ga, GaN, Ge, SiC processing.
- **DARPA SMART Program** (May 2026): Strategic Materials Accelerator at University of Utah — biotechnologies for REE extraction.

### European Union
- **CRMA**: 47 strategic projects inside EU (€22.5B capital) + 13 international (€5.5B).
- **Industrial Accelerator Act (March 4, 2026)**: "Buy European" discussion.
- **EU–US Action Plan (April 24, 2026)**: Reference price tools, border-adjusted price floors.
- **Funding gap**: EU ~€5B vs US ~€40B. No EU equivalent to DFC/EXIM.

### Asia-Pacific
- **Australia**: A$1.4B + US$2.2B joint financing for 11 named projects. Joined G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance (March 2026).
- **Canada (PDAC 2026)**: C$3.6B new programs — C$2B Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund, C$1.5B First and Last Mile Fund. 2-year approval timelines.
- **Japan**: Floor price agreement with Lynas extended to 2038 (March 2026).

---

## 4. Supply Chain Intelligence

### Production Announcements

| Company | Mineral | Development | Impact |
|---------|---------|-------------|--------|
| Mt Holland (SQM/Wesfarmers) | Lithium | Expansion approved — 4.4M t/yr (2×) | Bearish supply |
| Mt Marion (MinRes/Ganfeng) | Lithium | FID: $490M AUD flotation plant + UG mine | Bearish supply |
| Bald Hill (MinRes) | Lithium | Restart after 18-month suspension | Bearish supply |
| Core Lithium (Finniss) | Lithium | Operations restarting | Bearish supply |
| SEMCORP (Malaysia) | Battery | $2B separator project terminated | Bearish demand signal |
| Eramet Weda Bay | Nickel | Ceased — RKAB quota cut 71% | Bullish nickel |
| Grasberg (Freeport) | Copper | Force majeure since Sep 2025 | Bullish copper |
| Northern Graphite | Graphite | Spot sales moved to Metalshub | Signal for ex-China pricing |

### Processing Bottlenecks
- **Sulfuric acid crisis**: China H₂SO₄ export ban + Strait of Hormuz tensions disrupting ~50% of seaborne sulfur flows. Threatens SX-EW copper (~17% of global) and HPAL nickel processing.
- **Copper smelter crisis**: 2026 TC/RC benchmark at $0/t. Spot rates at negative $45–70/t. Smelters paying mines for ore.
- **REE separation**: Non-China capacity 5–10 years away. US DoD invested $439M+ since 2020.
- **Graphite anode**: Building outside China costs 3–10× more; qualification takes years.

### Company News
- **Altilium**: Filed patent for EcoMineral™ process (Cu from tailings). Established ReOre Technologies.
- **Nth Cycle + Ionic Rare Earths**: Electro-extraction replacing Chinese oxalic acid. Belfast integration Q4 2026.
- **Idaho Strategic Resources**: $1M DOE award for REE (Nd, Pr, Dy) from Idaho minerals.
- **Syrah Resources**: 24kt Q1 2026 at Balama; targeting first AAM sales from Vidalia, Louisiana H2 2026.
- **NextSource Materials**: Supply deal with Syrah for Abu Dhabi BAF (34–68kt fines over 7 years).
- **Valor (ex-Glencore, UIUC)**: Electrochemical liquid-liquid extraction — first facility in Houston. Covers Au, Cu, Pt, Ni, REEs.

---

## 5. Technology Watch

### Recycling & Processing Breakthroughs
- **INL EC-Leach (March 2026)**: >95% Li, Co, Ni, Mn recovery from batteries using electricity. 75% less energy, 88–90% less chemicals.
- **Nth Cycle electro-extraction**: Replaces Chinese-sourced oxalic acid in REE refining. Eliminates hidden chemical supply chain dependency.
- **Supra Elemental Recovery (UT Austin)**: 3D-printed reusable molecular-sponge cartridges for Co, Li, Ga, Sc from tailings/e-waste.
- **Altilium EcoMineral™**: Up to 70% Cu leaching from 110M-tonne tailings using biodegradable lixiviants. Near-neutral pH, ambient pressure.
- **DARPA SMART Program** (May 2026): University of Utah test bed for biotechnologies to extract REEs from phosphate mine waste, acid mine drainage, and e-waste. First users: DARPA's EMBER program (microbial REE separation).

### Substitution
- **Al-for-Cu debate**: ~70% of 2023 global copper consumption replaceable by aluminium. Barrier is entrenched reputation.
- **Sodium-ion batteries**: CATL scaling to 40 GWh by end-2026. Hard-carbon anodes eliminate graphite.
- **Solid-state batteries**: Compatible with ternary (NCM) chemistry — sustaining Co/Ni demand.

### Exploration Tech
- **Silex (UK)**: Modular micro-refineries for REE recovery from industrial waste streams.
- **Supercritical fluid extraction (WashU)**: scCO₂/scN₂ processes achieving ~100% purity REE from coal fly ash.
- **Magnetic separation from granite waste (Italy)**: Recovery of REEs, Y, Sc, Li from extractive waste.

---

## 6. Outlook & Risk Assessment

### Key Risks to Monitor This Week

| Risk | Level | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| China REE control suspension expiry | HIGH | Nov 10, 2026 — expanded controls with extraterritorial reach could be reinstated |
| US critical mineral tariff deadline | HIGH | July 13, 2026 — 180-day review; potential tariffs on processed Chinese minerals |
| Lithium supply restarts | MED | Mt Holland/Mt Marion/Bald Hill/Finniss all adding supply — ceiling forming at ¥190–210k |
| Sulfuric acid / copper crisis | MED | China H₂SO₄ ban + Strait of Hormuz threatens SX-EW output (~17% of global Cu) |
| Indonesia nickel quotas | MED | Potential Q3 supplemental issuance could cap nickel price |
| DRC political stability | MED | Contract audits and elections creating uncertainty |

### Price Forecast Signals
- **Lithium**: Near-term correction from supply-restart news. Medium-term bullish (¥190–210k floor). CITIC/UBS ¥250–298k vs Goldman sees H1 peak.
- **Cobalt**: Strongly bullish — structural deficit entrenched. Limited substitution options near-term.
- **Nickel**: Moderately bullish — policy cuts offset by high LME inventories (~250kt).
- **Copper**: Structurally bullish — deficit consensus 150–400kt. AI/electrification creating unprecedented demand. New supply 5–10 years away.
- **REE**: Ex-China premium (4–6×) to persist until Western separation comes online (late 2020s).
- **Graphite**: Near-term oversupply masks long-term structural tightness. Ex-China demand growing 14% annually.

### Geopolitical Flashpoints
1. **Nov 10, 2026** — China REE control suspension expiry (most consequential single catalyst for heavy REEs)
2. **Synchronised resource nationalism cluster** — DRC + Indonesia + Zimbabwe + China + Namibia
3. **US–China mineral trade war escalation** — Project Vault + potential July tariffs
4. **Strait of Hormuz / Iran** — Cascading sulfuric acid crisis into copper production
5. **EU funding gap** — US deployed 8× EU CRM funding. Europe risks falling behind in supply security

### Thematic Observation
The critical minerals landscape is shifting from **policy announcements to execution risk**. Western governments have deployed massive financial tools ($120B Vault, €40B+ US project support, C$3.6B Canada, A$1.4B Australia) but the 15+ year lead times for new mines and 5–10 year timelines for processing capacity mean supply-demand tension persists through the 2030s. The real action is moving to the **midstream** — the race to build non-Chinese processing, separation, and refining capacity.

# EDGE Critical Minerals Intel — Weekly Brief
**Date:** 2026-05-27
**Report Period:** May 25–27, 2026
**Week:** 3

## Executive Summary

- **Lithium corrects 14% from ¥205k peak** as supply-restart announcements (Mt Holland, Mt Marion, Bald Hill, Finniss) spook the market. GFEX futures at ¥168,960/t, spot at ~¥179,700/t. Underlying battery demand remains robust (+55.6% YoY) but supply psychology has shifted bearish.
- **Cobalt holds at $56,290/t**, flat w/w, as DRC quotas continue to constrain supply. Nickel steady at $18,560/t. Sulfuric acid crisis (China export ban + Strait of Hormuz) threatens SX-EW copper output and HPAL nickel processing costs.
- **JPMorgan warns of 330,000-ton copper shortfall** in 2026 — AI data centres (~475kt demand), EV scaling, and grid modernisation driving a "triple demand threat." LME copper at $13,624/t. TC/RC benchmark at $0/t.
- **DARPA launches SMART program** for strategic materials at University of Utah. DOE's $69M Critical Minerals Accelerator NOFO opens for industry-led pilot/demo projects. Nth Cycle + Ionic Rare Earths partnership to replace Chinese oxalic acid in REE refining.
- **Resource nationalism continues on five fronts** — DRC cobalt quotas, Indonesia nickel cuts, Zimbabwe lithium quotas, Namibia raw mineral export ban, China expanded REE controls — creating compounding supply chain pressure across minerals.

---

## 1. Market Movements

### Lithium
- **GFEX LC2606 futures**: ¥168,960/t (down 14% from May 13 peak of ¥205,260/t). **Spot battery-grade**: ~¥179,700/t.
- **Warehouse warrants accumulating**: ~132,000 t on GFEX (+28%), contributing to bearish sentiment.
- **Supply-restart wave**: Mt Holland expansion approved (4.4M t/yr, 2× current); Mt Marion FID ($490M AUD for flotation plant + underground mine); Bald Hill restart after 18 months; Core Lithium Finniss restarting; SEMCORP terminated $2B Malaysia separator project.
- **Bullish supply factors still active**: Zimbabwe export quotas (no ore until late July); Jiangxi clay mine license renewals (7,500 t/yr LCE at risk); Greenbushes FY2026 cut by ~20kt LCE; Chile exports -5.1% MoM.
- **Demand**: April battery output 183.9 GWh (+55.6% YoY); May +10.5% MoM. ESS now 31% of lithium demand.
- **Analyst divergence**: CITIC ¥250k/t in 2–3 months; UBS ¥298k/t. Market consensus shifting toward near-term pullback then medium-term bullish.

### Rare Earth Elements
- **China's expanded controls (12 REEs)**: Suspended until November 10, 2026 — legal architecture intact. Extraterritorial "50% penetration rule" applies to foreign entities using Chinese-origin materials.
- **Separation bottleneck**: China controls ~90% of global separation capacity, ~93% of magnet production. Non-China buildout faces 5–10 year timelines.
- **DARPA "SMASH" Program**: 48-month, two-phase program to recover all ~80 stable elements from ore with near-zero waste.
- **Ucore RapidSX**: $4M DoD demonstration + $18M Louisiana facility. Column-based separation ~3× faster.
- **Nth Cycle + Ionic Rare Earths**: Electro-extraction to replace oxalic acid (sourced from China) in REE refining. Integration at Belfast facility from Q4 2026.
- **Price bifurcation**: Ex-China processed REEs command 4–6× Chinese domestic prices. NdPr elevated on US defense stockpiling.

### Cobalt & Nickel
- **Cobalt (LME)**: $56,290/t (flat w/w). DRC 96,600 t/yr export quota (~55% cut) continues to drive structural deficit of 36,000–91,000 t projected for 2026.
- **Nickel (LME)**: $18,560/t (flat w/w). Indonesia mining quotas cut ~30% (379M → 260–270M wmt). Eramet Weda Bay remains offline.
- **Sulfuric acid crisis**: China banned H₂SO₄ exports (May 1), threatening HPAL nickel processing costs in Indonesia.
- **Battery chemistry**: LFP now ~81% of China power battery installations. High-nickel NCM remains essential for premium EVs.

### Copper
- **LME Copper**: $13,624/t (down $44 w/w). Near record highs.
- **Deficit estimates**: JPMorgan 330kt, UBS >400kt, ICSG ~150kt for 2026.
- **Demand**: AI data centres ~475kt in 2026 (+110kt YoY). EVs use 3–4× copper vs ICE. Grid modernisation accelerating globally. S&P Global projects 50% demand increase by 2040 (28M → 42M tonnes).
- **Supply**: Ore grades declining below 0.6%. New mines take ~17 years from discovery to production. Grasberg force majeure, Kamoa-Kakula guidance slashed. TC/RC 2026 annual benchmark at $0/t; spot at negative $45–70/t.

### Graphite & Battery Minerals
- **Natural graphite**: Flake prices depressed (~$800–1,200/t). Supply growth (966kt → 1.6Mt) outpacing demand.
- **Synthetic graphite**: Prices trending modestly upward (~$2,500–4,000/t) on tight capacity and rising coke costs.
- **China control**: ~90% of global anode production, ~98% of graphitization capacity.
- **US anti-dumping**: 93.5% on Chinese anode-grade graphite (July 2025) — procurement patterns not yet shifted.
- **Northern Graphite**: Moved majority of spot sales to Metalshub (March 2026) — signal of non-Chinese price discovery.
- **Sodium-ion**: CATL targeting 40 GWh capacity by end-2026; could reduce graphite demand intensity at the margin.

---

## 2. Geopolitical Developments

### US–China Rivalry
- **FORGE Initiative**: 54 countries + EU, succeeding Minerals Security Partnership. Korea first rotating chair.
- **Project Vault**: $120B strategic stockpile. Minimum pricing/tariff walls under discussion by USTR.
- **21 bilateral CRM frameworks** signed since Trump's return; 17 more under negotiation.
- **MP Materials**: $400M DoW investment + $150M loan for heavy REE separation at Mountain Pass. 10-year NdPr floor of $110/kg.
- **China's 15th Five-Year Plan** expected to prioritise strategic materials self-sufficiency, reducing technology transfer.

### Resource Nationalism Wave
- **Synchronised restrictions**: DRC (cobalt quotas), Indonesia (nickel cuts), Zimbabwe (lithium quotas), Namibia (raw mineral export ban + 51% local ownership proposal), China (REE controls).
- **OECD**: Export restrictions on critical minerals increased ~5× between 2009–2024.
- **"Third pole" emerging**: African leadership aligning with Middle Eastern capital (Saudi Arabia, UAE) to build processing capabilities outside US-China binary.
- **G20 Critical Minerals Framework** (2025 Johannesburg) formally endorsed "beneficiation at source."

### Russia & Central Asia
- Russia consolidating Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan) as secure resource hinterland for uranium, copper, rare metals.
- India cut Russian crude imports by ~800,000 bpd since Oct 2025 under US pressure.
- Three spheres of influence: China in Africa, US in Americas/Greenland, Russia in Central Asia — Europe structurally outside all three.

---

## 3. Policy & Regulation

### United States
- **One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025)**: $5B Industrial Base Fund, $2B National Defense Stockpile Fund, $500M/project Critical Minerals Loan Program.
- **Defense Production Act**: $550.4M FY2025 (up from $209.2M FY2024). Dept of War now lead agency.
- **Critical Minerals List expanded to 60**: boron, copper, lead, met coal, phosphates, potash, rhenium, silicon, silver, uranium added.
- **Jan 2026 proclamation**: 180-day deadline (July 13, 2026) for processed critical mineral trade deals — potential tariffs.
- **DOE Critical Minerals Accelerator**: $69M NOFO (April 2026) for industry-led pilot/demo projects. Topic Area 2: Ga, GaN, Ge, SiC processing.
- **DARPA SMART Program** (May 2026): Strategic Materials Accelerator at University of Utah — biotechnologies for REE extraction.

### European Union
- **CRMA**: 47 strategic projects inside EU (€22.5B capital) + 13 international (€5.5B).
- **Industrial Accelerator Act (March 4, 2026)**: "Buy European" discussion.
- **EU–US Action Plan (April 24, 2026)**: Reference price tools, border-adjusted price floors.
- **Funding gap**: EU ~€5B vs US ~€40B. No EU equivalent to DFC/EXIM.

### Asia-Pacific
- **Australia**: A$1.4B + US$2.2B joint financing for 11 named projects. Joined G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance (March 2026).
- **Canada (PDAC 2026)**: C$3.6B new programs — C$2B Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund, C$1.5B First and Last Mile Fund. 2-year approval timelines.
- **Japan**: Floor price agreement with Lynas extended to 2038 (March 2026).

- **Copper smelter crisis**: 2026 TC/RC benchmark at $0/t. Spot rates at negative $45–70/t. Smelters paying mines for ore.

- **Graphite anode**: Building outside China costs 3–10× more; qualification takes years.

- **Al-for-Cu debate**: ~70% of 2023 global copper consumption replaceable by aluminium. Barrier is entrenched reputation.
